ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory dual-layer screening at pre-incorporation: (i) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons classification under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC guidance, applied to all directors, officers, significant shareholders (≥25%) and the master franchisor; (ii) adverse-list screening against the UN Consolidated List, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c. 21, s. 12, the OFAC SDN List, and global debarment lists; enhanced due diligence required where a PEP holds ≥10% of voting shares or board control; all screening results must be recorded in the corporate records for FINTRAC inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (online filing via authorized service providers under the Alberta Corporate Account system; federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate legal name must be in English, French, or a combination of both using Latin script; Chinese-character trade names cannot be registered as the juridical name, but may be used as an unregistered brand/style name in parallel; any Chinese name must be transliterated into Latin script for the NUANS name search. The legal name must include a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element ('Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation' or abbreviations 'Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.'); the NUANS report must cover proposed variants and the name cannot be confusingly similar to any existing registered name, protected trademark, or stored-name reservation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada (suffix implying federal government or CBCA status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Alberta Director of Corporate Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must (i) obtain written reasons, (ii) file revised Articles of Incorporation with a new nominative variant within the remaining NUANS validity window, or (iii) submit a formal reconsideration request to the Director within 30 days; there is no monetary extension of the 90-day NUANS report, so a fresh search and reservation must be purchased after expiry. If refusal is upheld, judicial review may be sought before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. For federal CBCA alternatives, a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporations Canada must be filed within 21 days, with judicial review in the Federal Court as the final remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this industry. Alberta requires a physical street address in Alberta (no P.O. Box) as the registered office, and a registered records office (may be the same location) where the minute book, shareholder registers and ISC register are physically maintained and accessible during ordinary business hours; a commercial virtual-office service with an Alberta physical address and document-access facilities satisfies the statutory test, and the boba-tea franchise industry does not attract enhanced substance or physical-presence requirements beyond standard registered-office obligations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (quantified risk of unannounced corporate-registry inspection: <10% over a 3-year rolling horizon); Alberta Corporate Registry does not routinely conduct physical inspections of registered offices for private corporations, although municipal business-licence officers and Alberta Health Services may inspect the franchise locations for food-safety compliance; inspection risk rises only upon third-party complaint or failure to maintain registered office documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended (ABCA), including in particular the provisions governing articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, corporate name and distinctiveness, registered office and records, share capital and allotment, directors and officers, and annual returns; supplemented by the regulations made thereunder. A federal alternative under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, with extra-provincial registration in Alberta, is available but is not adopted by this SOP.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Registry of Corporations), Service Alberta, online business services portal and authorized service providers
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form ICA-1) filed electronically with the Alberta Corporate Registry, followed by issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or deposit requirement under the ABCA. The articles may authorize shares with or without par value; consideration for shares may be cash, property, or past services as determined by the directors. A nominal-par or no-par common share structure is recommended for the franchise holding and syrup supply operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED: The subscribers listed in the Subscription List are allotted the aggregate number of common shares described therein, full lawful consideration having been received.

RESOLVED: The registered office is fixed at [Registered Office Address], [City], Alberta, and [Corporate Services Provider] is appointed registered agent for service of process.

RESOLVED: [Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until successors are duly appointed.

RESOLVED: The directors are authorized to open bank accounts, file tax registrations, secure food establishment permits, municipal business licenses, and all other regulatory approvals for the Corporation's boba tea franchising and syrup supply operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Name Reservation Service (Service Alberta online portal or authorized NUANS service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a distinctiveness search through the Alberta Name Search system and procure a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report for the proposed corporate name. The name must contain a distinct element, a descriptive element where required, and a mandatory legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Limited', or 'Incorporated'. Submit the name reservation application online; a reserved name is held for up to 90 days. If the franchise brand is included in the corporate name, attach the franchise brand licensor's written consent or trademark registration evidence to avoid refusal based on confusion with an existing mark.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report issued within the preceding 90 days
List of proposed corporate names in descending priority order
Franchise brand licensor consent or trademark registration certificate where the brand name is used
Government-issued identification of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses or queries the name, review the statement of refusal, modify the distinct element, and re-submit an amended name search application; a corrected application within the same review cycle generally incurs no additional name search fee. Alternative names from the priority list may be selected without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form ICA-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Registrar of Corporations (online incorporation application portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form ICA-1 electronically through the Alberta Corporate Registry portal. Specify the number of directors (minimum one), the classes and maximum number of authorized shares (recommended: an unlimited number of common voting shares), any restrictions on share transfers (standard board-consent restrictions for a closely held franchise corporation), the Alberta registered office address, and the full names and residential addresses of the first directors and registered agent. Attest to the required due-diligence declarations, pay the statutory filing fee of CAD $100, and receive the electronically issued Certificate of Incorporation and filed Articles with the corporation number immediately upon acceptance.
required_dossiers: Completed and executed Articles of Incorporation (Form ICA-1)
Approved name reservation certificate or NUANS report
Personal information and consent forms for each first director
Registered office address located in Alberta
Regulatory and tax due-diligence attestation forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the registry issues a deficiency notice identifying the non-compliant clauses; correct the articles and re-submit within 60 days without loss of the name reservation, or refile with the applicable fee if the deficiency is material. Urgent corrections may be escalated through the Corporate Registry online service request system.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Registered Agent Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a physical civic address in Alberta and may not be a post-office box. The registered agent may be an individual resident in Alberta or a corporation authorized to transact business in Alberta. The registered office and registered agent named in the Articles come into force on the certificate date. Execute the consent of registered agent and annex it to the Articles, and put in place a registered agent service agreement confirming the agent will accept service of process and statutory notices on behalf of the Corporation.
required_dossiers: Consent of Registered Agent to Act (signed individual or corporate agent form)
Registered Agent Services Agreement
Form ICA-2 (Change of Registered Office) where the office address differs from that stated in the Articles
Confirmation of the physical civic address in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent resigns or the address is invalidated, appoint a successor agent and file the applicable notice with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days. If the registry rejects the address as a non-locatable civil address, provide a civic address certificate or land description issued by the municipal authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organization — First Board Resolution, Share Allotments, and Statutory Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate governance (board of directors and subscribers); no government filing required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, convene the first directors' meeting or adopt the pro-forma written resolution set out in the incorporation legal framework. Approve the allotment and issuance of common shares to subscribers, open corporate bank accounts, adopt the by-laws of the Corporation, fix the financial year end, appoint officers, and authorize signing authorities. Instruct corporate counsel to prepare the registered minute book containing the Articles, Certificate of Incorporation, by-laws, consents of directors, first board resolution, share certificates, register of members, register of directors, and register of transfers, and to issue share certificates against the subscription funds held in trust.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (as set out in the incorporation legal framework)
By-laws of the Corporation
Directors' consent to act in office
Subscription list, share certificates, and share register or allotment ledger
Bank account resolution and authorized officers' signing mandate
Statutory minute book and corporate seal (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer is unable to serve, the remaining directors may pass a subsequent board resolution to appoint a replacement, execute a new consent, and file Form ICA-4 (Change of Directors) with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 15 days of the change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registrations — Business Number, GST/HST, Payroll, and Alberta Corporate Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online portal; Alberta Finance (corporate income tax administration through the CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a unique federal Business Number (BN) by registering online with the CRA. Open the GST/HST account (mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD $30,000; voluntary immediate registration is recommended to claim input tax credits on start-up franchise and equipment costs), open the payroll deductions program account before hiring employees, and open an import-export account for cross-border movement of boba tea ingredients and syrups. Register for Alberta corporate income tax through the CRA Business Number, as Alberta's 8% corporate income tax is administered on the federal corporate return; Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so no provincial PST registration is required. Register with the Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta for the food-service franchisor industry classification and obtain the WCB account number prior to staff deployment.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and filed Articles
Registered office address and directors' contact information
Fiscal year end election of the Corporation
Estimated annual taxable supplies for GST/HST threshold assessment
Directors' personal identification and proof of signing authority for CRA registration
NAICS 722515 business activity classification for the boba tea and syrup supply operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA returns a query on the Business Number application, respond through the CRA Business Account message centre with corrected legal name or registered office documentation; the CRA will reassess and activate the account within 10 business days. GST/HST account activation may be backdated to the commencement of business activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Health Services (AHS) — Environmental Public Health Division, in coordination with the municipal business licence department of the operating city or municipal district
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Permit issued under the Public Health Act, RSA 2000, c P-37, and the Food Regulation (Alta Reg 31/2006)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (Environmental Assessment and Regulatory Approvals Division)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report; retail boba tea preparation and franchise administrative offices fall below the mandatory thresholds of the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12, Schedule 1. A municipal development permit or project-specific environmental registration may be required where syrup blending or ingredient manufacturing volumes exceed municipal zoning thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with municipal sanitary sewer use bylaws, including fats, oils and grease (FOG) limits typically not exceeding 100 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), and total suspended solids (TSS) discharge limits applicable to food-service and non-alcoholic beverage operations; grease interceptor installation, sizing, and maintenance schedules are mandatory for preparation and blending premises. Solid food waste and packaging must be handled in accordance with the Waste Control Regulation (Alta Reg 192/1996), with commercial recycling and organic waste diversion where municipal programs apply. Refrigeration systems must comply with the Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbons Regulation (Alta Reg 132/2010); volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from cold-beverage and syrup handling are negligible, but any solvent-based cleaning agents must be stored and vented in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire department fire safety inspection and Fire Code certification under the Safety Codes Act, RSA 2000, c S-1, covering fire extinguishers, commercial suppression hood systems, and egress compliance for food-preparation areas; structural load inspection and building permit sign-off for refrigeration units, industrial blenders, and storage racking; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 and the Occupational Health and Safety Code, including a hazard assessment, WHMIS training records, and a written safety manual; Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta account registration and clearance certificate confirming no outstanding premiums; and employment standards registration with the Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade for payroll compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada) - national self-assessment tax administration. Portal: My Business Account and Business Registration Online at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Alberta corporate income tax is imposed under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act and its administration is consolidated with the CRA under the federal-provincial collection agreement announced in Alberta Budget 2024, effective for the 2025 and later taxation years. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) operates the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for export documentation and customs control.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Nexus determination: a Canadian business corporation (and any foreign parent or foreign licensor) making taxable supplies in Canada must register for GST/HST once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (Excise Tax Act ss. 148 and 240). Step 2 - Application: obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST program account (RT program code) through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; non-resident entities may file Form RC1/RC1X through a Canadian representative and must provide a Canadian address of records. Step 3 - Issuance: CRA issues the BN and RT reference number (e.g., 123456789 RT0001), which functions as the statutory VAT ID for Canadian sales, imports, and export zero-rating. Step 4 - Income tax accounts: the corporation must also open an RC (corporate income tax) program account and file an annual T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, which reports both federal Part I tax and Alberta corporate tax (Alberta general rate 8%; Alberta small business rate 2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a Canadian-controlled private corporation). Step 5 - Permanent establishment: a non-resident franchisor operating through an Alberta permanent establishment opens a PE program account and allocates Alberta-source taxable income on the T2, with treaty relief evaluated against the Canada-foreign tax treaty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer under Income Tax Act s. 2(2) and does not qualify for US-style check-the-box or pass-through treatment. The Alberta-incorporated entity is resident in Canada by virtue of central management and control being located at its registered office, and it is taxed on worldwide income with foreign tax credit relief. The boba tea global franchise entity may qualify as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) if Canadian residents own 50% or more of the voting shares or equity; otherwise it is classified as a non-resident-owned private corporation or another corporation for T2 purposes. Franchise royalties from foreign licensees remain taxable at the corporate level in Canada, subject to applicable treaty reductions. No tax-exempt zone or general tax holiday applies in Alberta for beverage franchise operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box classification regime; the following statutory elections and disclosures are relevant to an Alberta boba tea global franchise holding corporation: (i) Excise Tax Act s. 156 election for closely related corporations, deeming intra-group supplies (including royalty and syrup transfer charges) to be made for nil consideration, eliminating GST/HST on inter-corporate flows; (ii) ETA s. 179 drop-shipment election for qualifying goods sold to non-resident registrants; (iii) Income Tax Act s. 85 rollover election for tax-deferred transfer of intellectual property, franchise agreements, and syrup supply contracts into the Alberta corporation; (iv) ITA s. 85.1 share-for-share exchange election for restructuring the global franchise chain; (v) hybrid mismatch disclosure and deduction-denial rules under ITA ss. 18.4 and 18.5, which require structured arrangement reporting rather than an elective carve-out; (vi) CCPC and associated-corporation elections and disclosures filed with the T2 return, Schedules 9 and 12; and (vii) GST/HST annual filing election and quick method election where eligibility conditions are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. Alberta is a non-participating province, so only the 5% federal GST applies, without an Alberta provincial sales tax or provincial HST component. Supplies of boba tea beverages and merchandise in Alberta stores are taxable at 5%; exported syrups, tapioca pearls, powders, packaging, and franchise royalties supplied to non-resident franchisees are zero-rated at 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1); registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Non-resident suppliers of specified digital services and e-commerce supplies to Canadian consumers are subject to a separate simplified GST/HST registration regime with no de minimis threshold, but the Alberta store-based franchise entity operates under the standard CAD 30,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate. GST/HST is self-assessed; registrants file returns (Form GST34) through CRA My Business Account, GST/HST NETFILE, or approved EDI/API interfaces, and must retain electronic records in readable and machine-supportable format (ETA s. 286; ITA s. 230). The federal government is advancing a pan-Canadian PEPPOL baseline for voluntary B2B e-invoicing, but no federal or Alberta law compels pre-clearance of invoices before issuance. For exports, CBSA requires electronic export declarations through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for goods requiring permits, controlled goods, or goods valued over CAD 2,000 per shipment; CERS supports API/EDI filing but does not impose digital stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment at 0% GST/HST applies under ETA Schedule VI: Part V, s. 21 for goods exported from Canada, covering boba tea syrups, tapioca pearls, flavor powders, and packaging shipped to foreign franchisees, provided the supplier maintains an export evidence trail demonstrating physical export within a reasonable time; and Part VI, s. 7 for services supplied to non-residents, covering franchise royalties, trademark licensing, training, and management services rendered to overseas franchisees, provided the recipient is a non-resident, the service is not performed for consultation? use or consumption in Canada, and the franchisee is not a GST/HST registrant. Tangible property supplied to a non-resident intermediary may qualify under the drop-shipment rule in ETA s. 179. The franchise entity may claim full input tax credits on inputs attributable to zero-rated exports, generating a refundable net GST/HST position, provided contemporaneous agreements, customs, transport, and payment records substantiate the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or G13 Export Declaration for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000
Commercial invoice with HS classification, FOB/CIF valuation, country of origin, and explicit zero-rated export notation
Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or truck/cargo manifest evidencing physical departure from Canadian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC), SWIFT MT103, or bank payment record evidencing settlement from the non-resident franchisee
Executed franchise or license agreement and royalty schedule demonstrating supply to a non-resident and use of intellectual property outside Canada
Packing list, delivery order, and shipping instructions substantiating the foreign destination and consignee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and CBSA jointly scrutinize zero-rated export claims and may reassess within the default four-year statutory period, which is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation, willful neglect, or fraud is established (ETA s. 298). Unsupported export claims are reclassified as taxable at 5% GST, subject to arrears interest at prescribed rates and reversal of all claimed input tax credits, with penalty exposure under ETA s. 280 for failure to file returns, ETA s. 285 for false statements or omissions (the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the federal tax sought to be evaded), and ETA s. 286 for knowing evasion, including fines and imprisonment on summary conviction or indictment. Retroactive clawbacks also apply where franchise royalty zero-rating is found to involve a related Canadian-resident recipient or intellectual property used in Canada. Canada does not impose a formal statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day default reflects CRA administrative expectations for export evidence and cross-border payment settlement, and it is used as the internal compliance threshold for maintaining the export substantiation file.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) (monetary authority and payment-systems oversight); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) (prudential regulator for Schedule I-III banks); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) (AML/ATF and large-transaction reporting); Payments Canada (operator of Lynx RTGS, ACSS, and Real-Time Rail); Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) (Investment Canada Act notification and review).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII; no exchange-control permits, repatriation quotas, or central-bank pre-approval for inward or outward remittances. Profit remittance is restricted in practice only by corporate-law solvency tests and by Part XIII withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents (default 25%; treaty-reduced, e.g., 5-15% for dividends and 10% for industrial royalties under the Canada-US Tax Convention). Compliance encumbrances are reporting-only: FINTRAC reporting for transactions of CAD 10,000 or more (including same-day aggregation), FATCA/CRS account disclosures, and Statistics Canada balance-of-payments surveys. The Alberta bubble-tea franchise platform is classified as a standard low-risk commercial treasury profile, not a restricted sector under the Bank Act or the Investment Canada Act service-sector rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no designated custodian requirement for franchise-royalty or syrup-export proceeds. Foreign-currency receipts (USD, CNY, TWD, MYR) may be held in foreign-currency accounts at a Schedule I bank or converted to CAD at commercial discretion. Only FINTRAC large-transaction reporting, FATCA/CRS classification, and Statistics Canada trade-survey filings attach to these flows; no central-bank approval or surrender order is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Canada has no EU-style EMI passporting regime; non-bank payment service providers are subject to Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration (operational since 2024) and FINTRAC money-services-business registration. Offshore UK-FCA or EU-authorized EMIs are permissible only as ancillary rails: they cannot offer Lynx/ACSS clearing membership, CDIC deposit insurance, interac acquiring, or trade-finance facilities, and must clear through a Canadian Schedule I bank. Primary treasury and escrow functions for the franchise platform must therefore reside at Schedule I banks, with EMIs limited to small-ticket cross-border supplier disbursements and legacy POS concentration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under PCMLTFA where the director or UBO completes video KYC with liveness checks and document verification and the corporation supplies a certified Alberta Corporate Registry extract and a board resolution designating signatories. In practice, Schedule I banks require at least one in-branch interview in Alberta for (i) capital-escrow balances above CAD 250,000, (ii) accounts with non-resident directors, or (iii) expected cross-border wire volume exceeding 20 wires per month. A fully offshore board without Canadian nexus will be declined unless a licensed Alberta legal or fiduciary agent (e.g., Dentons, DLA Piper, or a Big-4 corporate-services arm) is engaged as compliance intermediary and an authorized signatory attends in-province.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque multi-layer UBO structure (e.g., offshore intermediate holding companies above the Alberta operating corporation).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO register disclosure up to 25% interest, notarized passport copies of all natural-person owners, corporate charters and registry extracts for each intermediate entity, reference letters from a recognized FCA/FINTRAC/SEC-regulated institution, sworn source-of-wealth affidavit, and a signed group organizational chart evidencing the economic substance of the Canadian operating entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring franchise-royalty inbound wires lacking franchisee contract traceability (typology: unlicensed money-services business or third-party misappropriation).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Franchises Act-compliant franchise disclosure documents, executed franchise agreements per outlet, royalty fee schedule and calculation model, franchisee KYC files, and monthly royalty reconciliation sign-offs by the CFO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High outbound wire frequency to TWD/CNY/MYR suppliers of syrup concentrate and packaging materials (typology: trade misinvoicing or sanctions leakage).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed multi-year supply agreements, pro-forma invoices and purchase orders, transport documents (bills of lading, airway bills) with third-party inspection certificates, SWIFT field-70 reference to the underlying contract, and use of Commercial LC (UCP600) or documentary collection to sanitize the payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy POS receipts from franchised boba outlets aggregated into the corporate treasury account (typology: structuring under PCMLTFA or integration risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation of compliance, certified POS system-to-reconciler audit trail, daily sales ledger extracts by store, documented cash-handling and drop-safing policy, and SOC 1/2 reports from the franchise-management SaaS provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound parent equity and UBO injections route via SWIFT MT103 (field 70: 'CAPITAL INJECTION - SHARE SUBSCRIPTION' or 'FRANCHISE ROYALTY SETTLEMENT') to the designated Schedule I operating account. CAD-denominated injections clear same-day through Payments Canada Lynx; USD injections clear via the bank's New York correspondent and settle by internal FX conversion. Verification protocol: (i) match remitter against the UBO and shareholder register; (ii) retain board resolutions and share certificates evidencing issuance; (iii) classify the flow for Statistics Canada balance-of-payments surveys and CRS/FATCA reporting; (iv) file Investment Canada Act notification where a non-Canadian acquires control (2025 WTO-investor direct-acquisition review threshold: C$1.343 billion in enterprise value; non-WTO threshold: C$5 million in asset value); and (v) trigger FINTRAC large-transaction reporting for any single or aggregated credit of CAD-equivalent 10,000 or more.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 covering syrup-concentrate and equipment settlements; CAD corporate disbursements clear via ACSS (ACH) for payroll and recurring suppliers and via Lynx for high-value same-day obligations. Wholesale concentrate tranches above CAD 100,000 should be executed as irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) or documentary collections (D/P, D/A) with pro-forma invoice, certificate of analysis, bill of lading, and packing list. TWD/MYR/CNY beneficiary legs route through the Schedule I bank's international correspondent network; OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening applies to all beneficiary financial institutions; FINTRAC reporting applies at the CAD 10,000 threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/CNY) with tenors up to 24 months under ISDA 2002 or bank master FX terms
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CAD/USD CCS) to align franchise-royalty inflows with USD-denominated syrup procurements
Vanilla European FX options (CAD/USD call or put) with upfront premium for ring-fenced budget certainty
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on TWD, MYR, and offshore CNY where onshore deliverable markets are unavailable for regional franchisee-royalty collections
Rolling 30-day composite hedge programme layered on a Board-approved Royalty and Syrup Purchasing cash-flow forecast

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation (or the anniversary date of registration as an extra-provincial corporation), using the corporation's existing albertaregistries.ca account or authorized service provider.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100; continued failure to file annual returns for three consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution of the corporation by the Registrar under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation (the annual review date shown on the corporate register).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100; failure to file the annual return for three consecutive years can lead to administrative dissolution. In such a case the federal entity must be revived before the Alberta extra-provincial registration remains valid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each taxation year for the federal and Alberta provincial corporate income tax liability; the T2 return is the single filing window for both jurisdictions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance unpaid plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; interest on late or deficient payments; failure to file when required is an offence and may result in further penalties or legal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Corporate Income Tax Remittance and Annual Information Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency acting on behalf of Alberta Treasury Board and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the T2 deadline: six months after fiscal year-end; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA through the T2 return, with no separate Alberta return format for ordinary corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial corporate tax penalties and interest follow the CRA federal late-filing/instalment collection framework, and unpaid Alberta corporate tax is a recoverable Crown debt.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, every corporation must have an independent auditor unless a non-distributing corporation (private, no public securities outstanding) waives auditor appointment by unanimous shareholder consent for each financial year. There is no automatic revenue, asset, or employee-size exemption from the audit requirement. A distributing corporation or one whose shares are publicly traded must always appoint a public accountant and cannot use the unanimous waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS; private corporations generally apply the CPA Canada Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE / Canadian GAAP). Financial statements prepared for the statutory audit, shareholder approval, or CRA filing must be consistent with the chosen framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta requires the corporation to maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. The ISC register is not submitted with the annual return to Service Alberta; however, it must be kept on the corporation's records and updated within 15 days of any share transfer, pledge, or control event. The annual return updates only the corporate mailing address, directors, officers, and registered office information. Failure to maintain an accurate ISC register can lead to penalties under the ABCA and to inability to support future amalgamations, financings, or franchising disclosure certificates.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $120 - $400 USD per year for a registered office address service and service of process agent in Calgary, Edmonton, or a standard Alberta corporate/legal services provider; higher if the franchise uses a law firm as registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 - $25,000 USD per year for a small or medium-size private franchise holding company in Alberta under ASPE; if the unanimous shareholder waiver is adopted, a review engagement will normally cost between $4,000 and $10,000 USD.
